findings.title: Exit code 4 description is misleading
findings.body: The documentation for exit code 4 says 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.', but the actual behavior (see `printFeatureDisabled()` in `AbstractUpdatesCommand.java` and the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` in `UpdateCommandDistTest.java`) is that the command never runs at all and prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled.' Scripts that rely on exit code 4 to decide between rolling and recreate will be misled: the deployment may be perfectly eligible for a rolling upgrade; the code only signals that the user must enable the feature first. The row should describe 'Command unavailable: preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled' (or similar), not 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible'.

findings.title: Caution claim that the Operator will fail is inaccurate
findings.body: The CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' But the very next NOTE in the same section documents a default behavior that works without the feature: 'the update strategy defaults to mimicking Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior'. The Operator does not 'fail' when the feature is disabled; it only fails if the user supplies the new `spec.update.strategy` field without enabling the feature. The wording should be tightened to make that conditional explicit (e.g., '...must be enabled if you set `spec.update.strategy`').

findings.title: Breaking change of exit code for recreate upgrade (4 -> 3)
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from 4 to 3, and a new `FEATURE_DISABLED` constant took the value 4. Any external automation (CI/CD scripts, GitOps pipelines) that key off exit code 4 to detect 'recreate upgrade needed' will now interpret it as 'feature disabled' instead, taking the wrong branch. The previous public exit-code contract (4 == recreate, per the prior docs and code) is broken without a migration note. Either keep 4 as recreate and pick a new value for FEATURE_DISABLED, or call out the breaking change explicitly so downstream users can update their scripts.

findings.title: No test for `check` subcommand with feature disabled
findings.body: The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises the `metadata` subcommand (line 48: `@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME})`). The same feature gate was added to `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java lines 46-50), but there is no equivalent test for the `check` subcommand to confirm it also prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled.' and exits with code 4. A symmetric test (e.g., `testFeatureNotEnabledForCheck`) should be added.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4
findings.body: The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr error message; it does not verify that the process actually exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4). If a future change accidentally leaves the default 0 exit code, this test would still pass. The other tests in this file (e.g., `testCompatible` at line 75) do call `assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())`, so adding a similar exit-code assertion here would be consistent and catch regressions in the exit-code wiring in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`.

findings.title: YAML example uses non-YAML placeholder `Recreate|<not set>`
findings.body: The CR example shows `strategy: Recreate|<not set>`, which is not a valid YAML scalar and will be rejected (or stored as the literal string 'Recreate|<not set>') if a user copies the snippet verbatim. The pre-existing doc had the same issue and the PR was a natural place to fix it. The placeholder should be replaced with a valid value (e.g., a separate example with `strategy: Recreate` and a NOTE explaining that omitting the field means default behavior).

findings.title: printFeatureDisabled hard-codes the feature name in the error message
findings.body: `printFeatureDisabled()` hard-codes the literal string 'rolling-updates' in the message: `printError("Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled.");`. The method is now a reusable helper in `AbstractUpdatesCommand` and other preview-gated commands may follow the same pattern; if any of them is gated on a different feature, the message will be wrong. Either parameterize the method with the feature name, or rename it to something feature-specific (e.g., `printRollingUpdatesDisabled()`) so misuse is obvious.

findings.title: picocli.exit() does not halt execution; rely on `return` only
findings.body: In `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (and the identical block in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` at lines 46-50), the disabled-feature branch uses `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);` followed by `return;`. picocli's `CommandLine.exit(int)` only stores the requested exit code; it does not terminate the JVM or the run() method. The `return` is what actually prevents `validateConfig()` and the rest of the body from running. The code is correct, but the chosen API is misleading and a future refactor that drops the `return` (or calls `picocli.exit()` from a helper) would silently execute the rest of the command. Consider using `throw new ParameterException(...)` or letting the framework short-circuit, so the early-return contract is enforced rather than incidental.
